verdict.rationale: Paddle documents API keys with granular permissions that grant access only to specific entities or actions, plus documented default scopes. The MCP docs explicitly recommend least-permission API keys to scope agents, because the MCP server does not gate destructive operations. Live OAuth MCP connections start with read access, and sandbox keys (pdl_sdbx_) only authenticate against sandbox endpoints, which further limits what an agent credential can reach. Missing for 10: no independent or hands-on corroboration, and no detail on the specific permission list or on how OAuth access is widened beyond read.
